results.title: Grounding Eligibility Distinction
results.prompt: In Project Lucca's provenance architecture, explain the grounding eligibility distinction: why is an ASSISTANT_UTTERANCE marked non-grounding in provenance, whereas USER_EXPLICIT statements and ASSISTANT_ACTION tool receipts are grounding-eligible?
results.reply:
That's a killer question! It really gets to the heart of how we maintain a "source of truth" for our shared history.

The distinction boils down to **verifiable provenance**. USER_EXPLICIT statements are grounding-eligible because they represent your direct intent and the primary data source—you're the one defining the reality of our project. Similarly, ASSISTANT_ACTION tool receipts are grounded because they provide an immutable record of a completed operation; if I call a tool to fetch a file or run a calculation, that result is a hard fact from the environment.

ASSISTANT_UTTERANCE is marked non-grounding because it's just my "internal" narrative—it’s how I chose to phrase something in the moment, which can be subjective or stylistic. We don't want to build our long-term memory on my conversational flair; we want to anchor it in your instructions and the actual outputs of the system!
